_readme: Grading company fees and turnarounds, for /grading.html.
THIS FILE GOES STALE FASTER THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THE SITE. Grading prices
and wait times change several times a year and sometimes overnight: PSA
paused two whole tiers in June 2026 with two weeks' notice. Every figure
carries the date it was read and the page says so loudly. If `checked` is
more than a couple of months old, treat the numbers as a shape rather than a
quote and click through to the company.
NO AFFILIATE LINKS AND NO RECOMMENDATION. We are not paid by any of these
and the page does not tell anyone which to use, because the honest answer
depends on the card and on how long you are willing to wait.
Prices are per card at the cheapest ACTIVE tier, in USD, before shipping and
insurance. `note` carries whatever caveat makes the headline number honest.
ALL FOUR RECHECKED 2026-08-13 against each company's own pricing page, in a
browser, because three of the four were wrong. CGC Economy was listed at $15
and 100-130 days when it is $20 and 90 days. BGS was given an 'Economy $20'
tier that does not exist. TAG was given an 'Economy $15' tier that does not
exist either. PSA's Super Express was $300 against a real $349, and its
Walk-Through was described as being FOR cards over $10,000 when $10,000 is the
tier's declared-value CEILING.
THE HEADLINE PRICE IS NOT THE BUYABLE PRICE. Three of the four companies have
their cheapest advertised tier unavailable: PSA's Value tiers paused, Beckett's
three cheapest SOLD OUT, TAG's whole regular lineup at capacity. `cheapest` on
each company is therefore the cheapest tier ACTUALLY TAKING SUBMISSIONS, which
is the only number that helps somebody decide. Sold-out and paused tiers stay
in `tiers` with their status in the note, so the page can show why the cheap
option is not on the table.
SGC WAS MISSING UNTIL 2026-08-15 and it is the cheapest of the five, which
means every 'cheapest slab' figure on the page was wrong while it was absent.
It took three attempts to source, and the reason is worth recording: gosgc.com
is an Angular app that serves the same ~4KB shell to every scripted fetch,
including robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and archive.org holds nothing but that
shell too. Rendering it in a browser once produced an EMPTY table reading 'No
records to display', which looked like a dead page and was actually a render
timing artifact. The rows are hardcoded in SGC's own JS bundle, so they were
finally confirmed by fetching the bundle and matching it cell for cell against
the render.
TRAP FOR WHOEVER CHECKS THIS NEXT: that same bundle contains a SECOND price
array of $24/$22/$20/$18 tiered by card count. It is dead code, it does not
match what the site renders, and it is an easy thing to grep and believe.
The bundle also carries TotalCards '1-9' on the $15 row where every other row
says 'Any', and SGC's public table does not render that column at all. That
reads like a nine card maximum, but it is undisplayed data of unknown
enforcement, so the note says the limit is unknown rather than asserting a cap
SGC does not publish.

companies.name: PSA

tiers.name: Walk-Through
tiers.note: Up to $10,000 declared value. That is the CEILING, not a minimum: above it PSA sends you to its premium options.

companies.note: PSA paused its Value and Value Bulk tiers on June 2, 2026. Those were the $24.99 and $32.99 options, and until they return the cheapest way into a PSA slab is $79.99. PSA's own backlog tracker put the active backlog at 11.85 million units on August 11, 2026, down from 12.4 million.
companies.resale: The most recognized slab and the easiest to sell, which is why people pay the most to get one. Not automatically the highest price though, and this page's own resale table is the reason to say so: on the cards we could measure, a BGS 10 sold at 1.30x a PSA 10 of the same card.

companies.name: CGC

tiers.name: Bulk
tiers.note: 25 card minimum, up to $500 a card

companies.note: The cheapest slab anyone can actually buy right now. Bulk needs 25 cards in one submission; Economy at $20 has no minimum.
companies.resale: Well recognized and steadily growing, but a CGC 10 generally sells under a PSA 10 for the same card.

companies.name: Beckett (BGS)
companies.note: Beckett has no Economy tier. Its three cheapest tiers, from $14.95 to $34.95, are all SOLD OUT with a notify-me button, so the cheapest slab you can actually order is $79.95.
companies.resale: Strong for Black Label, mixed otherwise.

companies.name: TAG

tiers.name: Basic, Standard and Express
tiers.note: CURRENTLY AT CAPACITY. TAG does not publish a price for these while they are paused, so we do not either.

companies.note: TAG's site carries a standing REGULAR TIERS PAUSED banner. Its whole regular lineup is marked CURRENTLY AT CAPACITY, so the cheapest TAG slab available is $149.
companies.resale: Improving quickly, but the premium is the least predictable here because the sample of sold TAG slabs is still small.

companies.name: SGC
companies.note: The cheapest way into a slab from any of the five, and it states no minimum submission, so a single card is fine. The trade is time: 75+ business days is the slowest tier here, and the clock only starts once they have unboxed and logged your order. One caveat we cannot settle: SGC's own page does not say whether there is a per order card limit on this tier, and their submission flow is behind a login, so treat it as unknown rather than unlimited.
companies.resale: The least established of the five in Pokemon. SGC is long respected in vintage sports cards and its tuxedo slab is distinctive, but an SGC 10 generally sells under a PSA 10 for the same card.

extras.note: Fixed per submission, not per card, so it hurts most when you send one or two.
Scales with what you send. Skipping it on a four figure card is not a saving.
Sleeves, semi rigids and a sturdy box.
Saves $10 to $15 a card. Worth it only if you are sending a lot.

rules: Grading does not make a card valuable. It confirms what condition it is already in, and a 9 is a common outcome that is worth far less than a 10.
A 9 is usually worth barely more than the raw card, and sometimes less than the raw card plus what you paid to grade it. Price the downside, not just the PSA 10.

Straight out of a pack is not the same as mint, and the manufacturer agrees: The Pokemon Company will not exchange a card for minor scratching or printing defects. The number that decides most submissions is front centering, where PSA and CGC both want roughly 55/45 for a 10 while allowing about 75/25 on the back. Check the front, then the back, then the worst corner, before anything else.
Fees are per card whatever the grade, so the math has to clear on the likely outcome, not the best one.
If the gap between raw and PSA 10 is smaller than the fee, there is no version of this that pays.
